newsitem.title: UK: Britain's giant Millennium Wheel approved.
newsitem.headline: Britain's giant Millennium Wheel approved.

text.p: The world's largest fairground type wheel, to be built over the river Thames on London's south bank to mark the millennium celebrations, was given planning permission by Britain's Secretary of State for the Environment on Thursday.
The wheel is a joint venture between British Airways and the Millennium Wheel Company.
In answer to a parliamentary question John Gummer said "I have no plans to call in the planning application for the millennium wheel."
Gummer said, "the wheel is an inspired idea and an imaginative way to mark the millennium, providing unparalleled, once in a lifetime views of the heart of the capital."
In a separate statement British Airways said the 10 million pound landmark attraction should be turning by early 1999.

Some hail it as London's answer to Paris' Eiffel Tower or New York's Statue of Liberty. But others, including some members of parliament who will face it daily through the windows of parliament, think it will be an ugly blot on the landscape.
